entries.gave: Read the Cut, docs/product-vision.md as it stands, and both Mores; no inputs. Its people: the developers of invoicer, who build for the accounting team (print each client invoice without a developer) and for the developers who call the library from their own code and install the command once.
Read product-vision best-practice.md with template.md, and refactor-doc best-practice.md, to their end before any change.
The job, from the goal: invoicer gets each client invoice printed at that client tax rate from the invoice lines, and gives developers a library that gives the same results.
Two roles by the part of the job: the accounting team, who print each client invoice with the command; the developers, who call the library from their own code.
The accounting team prints only once someone installs the command; by the N1 decision 1 a developer installs it once, so the install stays with the developer role and needs no role of its own.
No person left unclear: the N1 decisions name both roles and who installs, so nothing to ask.
No split: within each role the members count the same result as their job done.
No merge: a printed invoice and unchanged results from their own code are different results.
Two roles, so neither is named user.

Each objective with its role as subject: O1 the accounting team bills each client; O2 the developers get the same results from their own code after each update of invoicer as before it, without editing their code; O3 the developers are left with a command they install once and never need to set up again.

Asked why: O2 went on from what their code does to what the developers get in their own work, the same results with no edits; O3 went on from the install task to what the developer is left with, a command needing no more setup.
Three distinct ends: a developer can keep same results without ever installing the command, and the accounting team can print without the library behavior a developer relies on staying put.

Tasks: O1 from starting a client invoice to holding it printed; O2 from updating invoicer to their own code giving its results again; O3 from starting the install to the command running for the accounting team with no setup after.
How well, as the share that fails: KR1.1 and KR2.1 kept; KR3.1 now also counts installs after which a developer sets the command up again, as O3 now names never needing to set it up again.
How fast: KR1.2 time to the printed invoice; KR2.2 edits a developer makes, their own effort, as the update time depends on their code; KR3.2 install time.
Each key result keeps Lower is better.
Ranking taken from the N4 decision: KR2.1, KR1.1 and KR3.1 come first, then KR1.2, KR2.2 and KR3.2, in the template paragraph.
No targets; the template sentence on Goodhart law stays.
Pieces of work from the decisions: printing from invoice lines with bad lines named; tax rate set at each print; the command calling the library that rounds tax one way; the one install.
Printing and the rate serve O1; the one rounding serves O2; the install serves O3, now worded as what the developer is left with, so printing stays O1 alone by the N5 decision.
Each pair has a piece serving one without the other, so no merge.
No piece names more than one objective, so nothing to split.
Every piece serves an objective, so nothing to ask.
The person gave the one way and the ideas; the N6 decision holds them, so nothing to ask.
The one way as decided: invoicer turns invoice lines into an invoice whose totals are right without anyone redoing the math.
The three ideas as the person worded them, each with what it gives toward O1 or O2.
Moments: install; start a client invoice from the invoice lines; a bad line; set the rate; print; developers update invoicer under their own code.
Each moment has an idea, except the install, which the N6 decision says takes no idea; no new idea proposed.
No idea proposed, so nothing to ask.
The three ideas each hold up the one way, within the template three; none dropped.
docs/product-vision.md read to its end: Roles says who each role is; Objectives and key results says each end and its measures; Concept says the one way and its ideas.
Readers: the developers of invoicer, who decide what to build and whether a change brought an objective closer.
The developers know invoicer, its library and Python; they come to learn whom it serves, each end, how to measure it, and the one way.
The three template sections are one topic each; no split.
Each item a reader looks for already has the template heading or its own list item.
Roles, objectives and ideas are items in no order, as bulleted lists; the ranking is an argument, in the template prose.
Readers words from the goal and the person: invoice lines, their own code, update invoicer, install, set up.
Chosen words: invoice lines, their own code, update invoicer, set up the command; no term to define.
Facts in two places: none; install once is said in Roles as the role job and in O3 as the end, which are different points.
No fact on the list, so no place to choose.
No two places differ, so nothing to ask.
Names: the developers and a developer for the role; invoice lines; their own code; the command; the library; update invoicer.
Each thing keeps one name; the objectives name the role the developers, as O1 names the accounting team.
No name refers to two things.

Took each Cut decision as it stands. Settled by the purpose and best practices: O2 and O3 wording with the developers as subject; KR3.1 also counts installs after which a developer sets the command up again; the ranking line written as the N4 decision names it. Nothing to ask.
